messages:
amanda.release: Heads-up: promo to prod is blocked — deploy-bot detected a manifest digest mismatch for api-service canary (2026-03). Can someone triage? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Promotion halted for image redwood/api-service:2026-03-canary. Manifest digest mismatch between staging (gcr.io/redwood-staging) and prod (gcr.io/redwood-prod). staging manifest sha256:aa11... prod manifest sha256:bb22...

chris.sre: Investigating. Quick guess: same layer contents but different compression metadata leading to differing layer digests on mirror push.

ben.infra: Confirmed with skopeo/regctl. Layer sizes match, digests differ. Example output: ```
$ skopeo inspect docker://gcr.io/redwood-staging/api-service:2026-03-canary --raw | jq '.layers[] | {size: .size, digest: .digest}'
{"size":1248123, "digest":"sha256:111aaa..."}
{"size":4096, "digest":"sha256:222bbb..."}
```
vs prod: ```
{"size":1248123, "digest":"sha256:333ccc..."}
{"size":4096, "digest":"sha256:444ddd..."}
```
Looks like compression/timestamp differences.

amanda.release: That'll trip our immutability checks. Short term plan? Pin? rollback?

chris.sre: Short term: pin promotion to last-known-good sha256:zz99good... I'll add a manual hold on the release.

ben.infra: Filing infra ticket. Likely cause: mirror push recompressed layers or builder gzip flags differ across build agents. We should standardize.

sara.oncall: I can re-push the exact canonical blobs from the artifact store using deterministic gzip flags (--no-name --no-time) to produce identical digests. Need approval to re-upload to prod mirror.

amanda.release: Approve. Pin the promo and do the re-push. We'll update release notes indicating the hold.

chris.sre: Plan: 1) pin promotion to sha256:zz99good... (done) 2) sara to re-push canonical blobs to prod with deterministic flags 3) registry-bot to verify manifests 4) if match, unhold and promote, else open infra rollback plan.

sara.oncall: Running re-push now. Command: ```
regctl image copy --no-compress --source gcs://builds/api-service/2026-03-canary.tar 
  docker://gcr.io/redwood-prod/api-service:2026-03-canary --gzip-opts=--no-name --gzip-opts=--no-time
```
I'll paste logs when done.

ben.infra: INFRA ticket drafted: "non-deterministic gzip metadata causing manifest digest drift across mirrors". Will attach skopeo outputs.

(3m later) sara.oncall: Re-push finished, uploads returned 200. Running skopeo inspect on prod image now.

sara.oncall: New prod layer digests: ```
{"size":1248123, "digest":"sha256:111aaa..."}
{"size":4096, "digest":"sha256:222bbb..."}
```
These match staging.

registry-bot: Manifest verification: staging manifest sha256:aa11... equals prod manifest sha256:aa11... 

chris.sre: Good. Re-run deploybot promotion check.

deploy-bot: Promotion preflight PASSED for redwood/api-service:2026-03-canary. No checksum mismatches. Ready to unhold.

amanda.release: Un-holding and promoting now. Release note snippet: "Canary promotion briefly held due to manifest digest mismatch caused by non-deterministic compression in push pipeline; resolved by re-pushing deterministic blobs. INFRA-7892 opened."

ben.infra: INFRA-7892 created with reproduction, logs, and recommended Buildkite plugin change to set deterministic gzip flags by default.

chris.sre: Postmortem actions: add nightly registry verification job to detect drift, and make deterministic-build flag default in canonicalization pipeline.

amanda.release: Thanks everyone. Marking resolved. :white_check_mark:

ben.infra: Leaving the pin for 15m of traffic validation before full traffic flip.

sara.oncall: 10m traffic check shows no errors.

amanda.release: Okay to close.

chris.sre: closing thread.
